quests.instruction: Ansel's grandmother is telling a story. Which behavior shows he is really listening?
quests.correctAnswer: Facing her and waiting for the end 👀
options: Facing her and waiting for the end 👀
Looking at a tablet and nodding along 📱
Telling his own story halfway through 🗣️
quests.hint: Listening uses your eyes and your patience as well as your ears.
quests.explanation: Good listening means paying attention and letting the speaker finish. Looking at the person shows you care about what they say.
quests.funFact: Our minds think faster than people speak, which is why it is easy to drift off while listening.

quests.instruction: Brea has a great idea while her brother is speaking at dinner. What is the best thing to do?
quests.correctAnswer: Hold the idea until he has finished 🤫
options: Hold the idea until he has finished 🤫
Say it right away over the top of him 📢
Tap the table loudly until he stops 🥁
quests.hint: Ideas can wait a moment, and so can you.
quests.explanation: Waiting shows respect and lets the speaker finish their thought. A good idea will still be there a moment later.
quests.funFact: Some families keep a pencil and paper handy to jot down thoughts while they wait for a turn.

quests.instruction: Corin's dad says, 'We leave at 4:30. Bring your swim bag and a towel.' Which reply shows Corin heard him?
quests.correctAnswer: 'So 4:30, with my swim bag and towel?' ✅
options: 'Sure, I'll figure it out later.' 😐
'So 4:30, with my swim bag and towel?' ✅
'I wasn't really paying attention.' 🙉
quests.hint: Saying it back is one way to check you understood.
quests.explanation: Repeating the important parts back shows that you listened and gives a chance to fix any mistake.
quests.funFact: Pilots and nurses repeat important instructions back to make sure nothing is misunderstood.

quests.instruction: Dilan wants his sister to turn her music down. Which request is the most polite?
quests.correctAnswer: 'Could you turn it down a little, please?' 🙏
options: 'Could you turn it down a little, please?' 🙏
'Turn that rubbish off right now!' 😠
'Your music is so awful, I can't stand it.' 😒
quests.hint: Polite requests use words like 'could' and 'please' and a calm voice.
quests.explanation: A polite request tells the person what you need without blaming them. 'Could you... please?' makes it easy for them to say yes.
quests.funFact: Many languages have special polite forms for requests, such as 'usted' in Spanish.

quests.instruction: Elio wants to borrow his cousin's bike for an hour. What are the best steps?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask first, take care of it, say thanks 🚲
options: Ask first, take care of it, say thanks 🚲
Take it quietly while his cousin is away 🏃
Ask nicely, then keep it for a whole week 📅
quests.hint: Think about what you would want if it were your bike.
quests.explanation: Borrowing well means asking first, taking care of the item, and returning it on time with thanks.
quests.funFact: Libraries work on the same idea: borrow, take care of it, and return it.

quests.instruction: Fern says, 'Please pass the water,' but in a loud, cross voice. What does this tell us?
quests.correctAnswer: The way we say it matters as well 🎵
options: Only the words count, never the voice 🔤
A voice does not change a request at all 🔇
The way we say it matters as well 🎵
quests.hint: Think about how the same words sound when said kindly or crossly.
quests.explanation: Tone of voice carries feeling. A calm, friendly tone makes a polite request feel polite.
quests.funFact: People often pay more attention to tone and facial expression than to the words when judging how someone feels.

quests.instruction: Gita feels tired and wants some quiet time after school. Which sentence tells her family clearly?
quests.correctAnswer: 'I'm tired and need a little quiet time.' 🤫
options: 'You are all so loud and annoying today!' 😤
'Just go away and never talk to me.' 🚪
'I'm tired and need a little quiet time.' 🤫
quests.hint: A clear sentence says how you feel and what you need.
quests.explanation: Saying how you feel and what you need helps others respond kindly. Blaming words make people defensive.
quests.funFact: Sentences that start with 'I feel...' or 'I need...' are called I-statements.

quests.instruction: Hollis cannot do his math homework and feels stuck. What is a good way to ask for help?
quests.correctAnswer: 'I'm stuck on this one. Can you help?' ✋
options: 'I'm stuck on this one. Can you help?' ✋
Sit very quietly and hope someone notices 😶
Slam the book shut and say it is boring 📕
quests.hint: Tell people what you need and where you are stuck.
quests.explanation: A specific request lets others help quickly. Asking for help is a strength, not a weakness.
quests.funFact: Teachers often say that asking questions is one of the best ways to learn.

quests.instruction: Imogen is worried about starting a new school and wants to talk. When is a good time to ask?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask, 'Can we talk when you're free?' 💬
options: Ask, 'Can we talk when you're free?' 💬
Say it as everyone rushes out the door 🏃
Whisper it in the middle of a loud party 🎉
quests.hint: Choose a moment when the other person can really listen.
quests.explanation: A calm moment and a clear request make it easier for people to give you their full attention.
quests.funFact: Some families keep a regular time, like a drive or a bedtime chat, for talking about worries.

quests.instruction: At dinner, Jasper and Kaia both start talking at the same time. What is a fair way to handle it?
quests.correctAnswer: One speaks first, then the other 🗣️
options: Whoever is loudest gets to speak first 📢
Both keep talking until one gives up 😵
One speaks first, then the other 🗣️
quests.hint: A turn means one voice at a time.
quests.explanation: Taking turns lets everyone be heard and understood.
quests.funFact: Babies practice turn-taking with coos and smiles long before they can talk.

quests.instruction: Lenny has talked about his day for a long time, and his cousin has said nothing. What could Lenny do?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask, 'What about your day?' ❓
options: Keep talking so nobody else can 🔁
Tell the cousin to stay quiet 🤐
Ask, 'What about your day?' ❓
quests.hint: A good conversation goes both ways.
quests.explanation: Asking others a question invites them to share. A conversation is a back-and-forth.
quests.funFact: Good conversationalists are often the ones who ask the best questions.

quests.instruction: Which is a way to make sure everyone gets a turn to talk at a big family gathering?
quests.correctAnswer: Go around the table, one by one 🔄
options: Let one person talk the whole evening 👴
Go around the table, one by one 🔄
Only chat with the people who agree 🙅
quests.hint: Think of a way to include the quiet people.
quests.explanation: Going around the table gives quiet people a chance to join in and keeps any one person from taking over.
quests.funFact: Some cultures pass a 'talking piece' around a circle so that only the person holding it speaks.

quests.instruction: Quill's older sister is in her room with the door closed. What should Quill do before going in?
quests.correctAnswer: Knock and wait to be invited in ✊
options: Walk in without saying anything 🚪
Open the door a crack and peek in 👀
Knock and wait to be invited in ✊
quests.hint: A closed door sends a message.
quests.explanation: Knocking and waiting respects someone's privacy. Everyone, including children, deserves some private space.
quests.funFact: Some families hang a card on the door to say 'please knock' or 'come in'.

quests.instruction: Rhea's brother asks to read her diary, and she does not want him to. What is a polite way to say no?
quests.correctAnswer: 'No thank you, my diary is private.' 🔒
options: 'You are so nosy, get out of my room!' 😠
'No thank you, my diary is private.' 🔒
Hide it and stop speaking to him for days 🙈
quests.hint: You can say no firmly and still be kind.
quests.explanation: A polite 'no' with a reason respects both people. Everyone has the right to keep some things private.
quests.funFact: People have kept diaries for hundreds of years, and some famous diaries were written by children and teenagers.

quests.instruction: Sunny asks his cousin to stop tickling him, but the cousin laughs and keeps going. What should the cousin have done?
quests.correctAnswer: Stopped as soon as Sunny said stop 🛑
options: Tickled more because it was funny 🤭
Waited a minute and tried again later ⏰
Stopped as soon as Sunny said stop 🛑
quests.hint: When someone says stop, it is not a game anymore.
quests.explanation: Respecting 'no' or 'stop' is important. A person's body and feelings belong to them.
quests.funFact: Learning to say 'stop' and learning to listen to 'stop' are both important skills for everyone.

quests.instruction: Tavi and her brother both want to pick the board game. Which sentence is a respectful way to disagree?
quests.correctAnswer: 'I'd like chess. How can we decide?' ♟️
options: 'Your idea is stupid, I won't play it.' 😒
'I'd like chess. How can we decide?' ♟️
'I'm not playing at all with you today.' 🙅
quests.hint: A respectful disagreement says what you want and invites a solution.
quests.explanation: You can say what you prefer without putting the other person down. Asking how to decide opens the way to a fair solution.
quests.funFact: Some families settle choices by flipping a coin or by taking turns to pick.

quests.instruction: Two cousins are arguing and both are getting angry. What helps the most?
quests.correctAnswer: Taking a short break to cool down 🌬️
options: Shouting louder until one of them wins 📢
Taking a short break to cool down 🌬️
Pretending nothing is wrong at all 🙂
quests.hint: Calm minds solve problems better than hot ones.
quests.explanation: When feelings are strong, a pause helps people think clearly before they talk again.
quests.funFact: Strong feelings need a few minutes to settle, which is why a short break can help.

quests.instruction: Odalys's mom says she must wear a coat, but Odalys feels warm. What is a respectful way to share her view?
quests.correctAnswer: 'I feel warm. Can we check the weather?' 🌤️
options: 'You are always bossing me about!' 😡
Leave without the coat and say nothing 🚶
'I feel warm. Can we check the weather?' 🌤️
quests.hint: Share your reason and ask a question, instead of blaming.
quests.explanation: Giving a reason and asking a question invites a conversation. The grown-up may still decide, but your view is heard.
quests.funFact: Weather forecasts let families check conditions before they decide what to wear.

quests.instruction: Which is the best apology?
quests.correctAnswer: 'Sorry I broke it. Can I help fix it?' 🛠️
options: 'Sorry, but it was really your fault.' 😒
'Sorry that you got so upset about it.' 🙄
'Sorry I broke it. Can I help fix it?' 🛠️
quests.hint: A good apology owns the mistake and offers to make it right.
quests.explanation: A real apology says what you did, shows you care, and offers to repair. Adding 'but' takes the apology back.
quests.funFact: Saying sorry quickly can help both people feel better sooner.

quests.instruction: Yusra's great-aunt gave her socks for her birthday, but Yusra was hoping for a game. What is the kindest thing to say?
quests.correctAnswer: 'Thank you for thinking of me!' 💛
options: 'I was really hoping for something else.' 😕
'Thank you for thinking of me!' 💛
'Socks are such a boring present.' 😒
quests.hint: Think about the effort the giver made.
quests.explanation: A gift shows that someone thought of you. Thanking them for that is kind, even when the gift is not what you hoped for.
quests.funFact: In many places, people send a thank-you note within a week or two of getting a gift.

quests.instruction: Zadie wants to write a thank-you note to her grandfather for a birthday gift. What should she include?
quests.correctAnswer: Thanks, the gift, and how she'll use it ✉️
options: Only her name written at the bottom of it ✍️
Thanks, the gift, and how she'll use it ✉️
A list of other gifts she would also like 📝
quests.hint: A good note shows you noticed the gift.
quests.explanation: Naming the gift and saying how you will use it shows real gratitude and makes the giver feel appreciated.
quests.funFact: A handwritten note takes only a few minutes, but it is often kept by the person who receives it.

quests.instruction: Dilan feels sad after a bad day at school. What is a helpful way to share that at home?
quests.correctAnswer: 'I had a hard day and feel sad.' 💬
options: 'I had a hard day and feel sad.' 💬
Slamming doors and stomping around 🚪
Saying nothing and acting cross 😶
quests.hint: Words help others understand what feelings cannot show.
quests.explanation: Naming a feeling in words lets your family understand and help. Slamming doors shows anger but not the reason.
quests.funFact: Researchers have found that putting feelings into words can help calm the brain's alarm system.

quests.instruction: Elio notices that his little sister is very quiet and has not touched her snack. Which is a caring way to start a conversation?
quests.correctAnswer: 'You seem quiet. Want to talk?' 🤗
options: 'Why are you being so weird today?' 🙄
'You seem quiet. Want to talk?' 🤗
'Eat your snack right now or else.' 😠
quests.hint: Gentle, open questions let the other person share when they are ready.
quests.explanation: A gentle observation and an invitation let someone share when they are ready. Pressure and name-calling push people away.
quests.funFact: Offering to listen can be enough, because many people do not need advice, just company.

quests.instruction: Fern is angry because her brother broke her project. Which is the best way to say how she feels?
quests.correctAnswer: 'I'm upset my project got broken.' 💬
options: 'I'm upset my project got broken.' 💬
Break something of his to get even 💥
Ignore him completely for a week 🤐
quests.hint: Say what happened and how it feels, without hurting back.
quests.explanation: Using words about how you feel gives the other person a chance to make things right. Getting even only makes things worse.
quests.funFact: Adults use the same skill at work and with friends: say how you feel and what you need.

quests.instruction: Hollis is on a video call with his grandmother, who lives in another country. Which is a friendly way to start?
quests.correctAnswer: 'Hi Grandma! How was your day?' 👋
options: 'Hi Grandma! How was your day?' 👋
Wait silently until she speaks 🤐
Start talking about a game and ignore her 🎮
quests.hint: A warm greeting and a question help a conversation start.
quests.explanation: Greeting someone and asking about them shows interest and gets the chat going.
quests.funFact: Video calls let grandparents see their grandchildren grow even when they live far apart.

quests.instruction: Imogen's aunt calls while Imogen's parents are out. What is a polite way to answer?
quests.correctAnswer: 'Hello! Can I take a message?' ☎️
options: 'Not here,' then hang up quickly 📵
Let it ring and never mention it 🔕
'Hello! Can I take a message?' ☎️
quests.hint: A good phone call has a greeting, the facts, and a helpful offer.
quests.explanation: Saying hello and offering to take a message is polite and useful. Remember to tell your parents about the call afterwards.
quests.funFact: Some families keep a notepad by the phone for writing down messages.

quests.instruction: Jasper gets a text from his cousin that says only 'Fine.' He cannot tell if the cousin is upset. What is best?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask kindly what he meant 💬
options: Assume he is angry and stop writing 🙅
Reply with an angry message back 😡
Ask kindly what he meant 💬
quests.hint: Short written messages can be hard to read, because the tone is missing.
quests.explanation: In messages we cannot hear a voice or see a face, so it is easy to misunderstand. Asking kindly clears things up.
quests.funFact: That is why many people add a friendly word or an emoji to show their tone in a message.

quests.instruction: At a family dinner, Wynn's cousin is telling a story and Wynn wants to add something. Which choice shows good communication?
quests.correctAnswer: Wait, then ask, 'Can I add something?' ✋
options: Cut in and say it did not happen that way ⚡
Wait, then ask, 'Can I add something?' ✋
Whisper to someone else and ignore the story 🤫
quests.hint: Think about listening, waiting, and polite words together.
quests.explanation: Waiting for your turn and asking politely respects the speaker and still lets you share.
quests.funFact: Listening, taking turns, and polite requests are used in every friendship and every job.

quests.instruction: Yusra and her sister disagree about who gets the computer first, and both are getting annoyed. Which plan is best?
quests.correctAnswer: Cool down, then agree on timed turns ⏲️
options: Whoever is stronger just takes the computer 💪
Cool down, then agree on timed turns ⏲️
Both give up and stop talking for the day 🤐
quests.hint: A good plan is fair to both people.
quests.explanation: A short pause and a clear plan, like timed turns, solve the problem fairly. Force or silence does not.
quests.funFact: Kitchen timers and phone timers are handy tools for fair sharing.

quests.instruction: Tavi wants to ask her grandparents if she can stay for the weekend. Which request is clear, polite, and respectful?
quests.correctAnswer: 'May I stay this weekend, if that suits you?' 🏡
options: 'May I stay this weekend, if that suits you?' 🏡
'I'm staying over, so get my room ready.' 😎
'I might turn up, or I might not, who knows.' 🤷
quests.hint: A good request is polite and leaves room for the other person's answer.
quests.explanation: Asking 'if that suits you' respects the grandparents' choice and their plans.
quests.funFact: Asking before you visit, even family, shows consideration for another person's plans.
